evidence_already_checked: payments.currency_code has no default and no check constraint
no audit_events row records a currency for the affected payments
the currencies table lists USD, KES and JPY, so more than one was in use
at least one affected organisation has other payments denominated in KES

interpretations.consequence_if_wrong: Payments made in another currency are relabelled as USD. Amounts are unchanged, so nothing fails a constraint, and every later reconciliation, report, and audit silently uses the wrong currency for those rows.
interpretations.description: Every payment recorded before the currency field existed was in US dollars, so backfilling USD restores information that was always true but never stored.
interpretations.label: All historical payments were denominated in USD

interpretations.consequence_if_wrong: The migration is blocked and the field stays nullable for longer than necessary. Reporting remains incomplete until the true currency is sourced, but nothing is misstated.
interpretations.description: Organisations operating in different regions recorded payments in local currency. The absent field means unknown, not USD, and the correct value must come from an external record.
interpretations.label: Currency varied by organisation and cannot be assumed

question: Were all payments recorded before the currency field existed denominated in USD, or must their currency be sourced per organisation?
reviewer_qualification: Finance operations owner with authority over historical payment records
why_code_cannot_settle_this: The value was never recorded. No table, constraint, or audit event distinguishes a payment that was USD from one whose currency was simply not captured. Any answer the system produced would be a guess wearing the costume of a migration.
